data.narrative:
Axion is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Daniel First and Rebecca Trachtenberg, having raised $62.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable, providing a reasonable baseline for peer positioning at this stage.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for Series B entry valuation and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $118M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—yields a median valuation of $1.75B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide spread reflecting material uncertainty about Axion's relative standing. The triangulated range is $100M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $934M. The stage-progression method suggests a more conservative valuation anchored to capital deployed, while peer medians reflect sector-wide pricing at Series B. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Axion's commercial traction and customer concentration align with the peer set, and whether the substantial heterogeneity within robotics and manufacturing warrants narrower comparables. Further diligence on revenue, retention, and technology differentiation would be required to refine this range.
